required_fixes: Candidate 4 omits an observed v1 behaviour that matters for authority: the workbench automatically resends a request once after HTTP 401, using a newly minted token, whatever the method (crates/rusty-core/src/session/worker/execution.rs:231-273). The only guards are that the environment is unchanged, the request is current, no newer Send exists and the app is not stopping. This conflicts with the accepted 'no silent replay of remote operations' and C15's 'no automatic replay'. Record it as observed reference. State that whether v2 drops it or requires re-admission/review before any resend of a managed or mutating request is a selected-design decision. Add a resend/replay case to the test surface.

Candidate 4 overstates how settled v1's 'managed-auth' classification is. In v1, managed_auth is inferred only from non-empty Options.redactions (execution.rs:221). The redirect rule therefore makes no distinction between tenant-managed credentials and workbench-owned secrets, which is the 'real variation' the candidate claims. Network::Live admits every destination (execution.rs:29-31), so v1 has no destination binding. The active<4 cap is in session/worker/execution.rs:107-110. State these precisely as observed facts and keep them separate from the proposed v2 policy.

Candidate 4's evidence for 'the inspected path does not connect generic managed-request execution to AIRS configuration review' should include the built-in SCM catalogue. It ships 81 POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE entries that resolve tenant credentials at Send (src/api_client/scm/catalog.json; scm/mod.rs:156-200). The HTML report cites catalog.json and src/ui/api_client/request.rs, but neither file is in source-inputs.json, and the Markdown cites rusty-core files instead. Make the two sets of citations consistent and fingerprint every cited file.

Candidate 1 does not address the existing draft-text/editor-truth seam. Under ADR 24, draft text deliberately stays in view editors behind the Form/DraftText/FieldFactory seam, and module-owned draft text was rejected because of render lag and two sources of truth. ADR 1/workspace.rs carry revision-based draft versions through Form, and ADR 27 has native editors own immediate input. Moving presentation to a React WebView changes where editor truth lives and how a fresh draft revision reaches Rust before review or Apply. Identify this as a friction point and a selected-design question (no concrete interface yet). Otherwise 'React presents state and operator intent' leaves review-validity binding unexplained.

Candidate 1 misplaces credential lookup. It is already GPUI-free in request::Client::send (src/request.rs:345-358), not in the native view; what the view holds is tickets/slots, protected-key IO and effect execution (gateway/tenant.rs:4-17, ADR 24). Correct the 'Before' wording. Name request::Client/Slot/Reads/Admission (ADR 2/16) explicitly as existing deep modules to retain. Separate the process-count cap (bridge::MAX_PROCESSES=4, which may be dropped) from Admission's behavioural rules that should be preserved or explicitly re-decided: interactive-before-read priority, deadline-from-submission for interactive work, cancelled queued reads never spawning, and per-product rate-limit containment (ADR 16).

ADR 0016 is cited as intent evidence for candidate 1 but is missing from source-inputs.json. Other cited claims also rest on files that are not fingerprinted: src/bridge.rs (MAX_PROCESSES), src/ui/harness/connection.rs (engine PATH), src/academy.rs (device authorization), and Academy topbar.tsx/use-theme-preference.ts/appearance-sync.tsx/notifications-bell.tsx. Add revision-pinned hashes for every file a candidate's claim depends on, and update checks.json's source_reference_files count.

Candidate 3 needs the missing evidence for 'not a full engine rewrite / reseal only native resources'. The v1 host puts the packaged bin/ (Node) and managed-cli/ (airs-cli) on the engine's PATH (src/ui/harness/connection.rs:772-785). The engine's own base instructions name airs-cli (airs_desktop_runtime.rs:104). The pin requires protocol 'airs-desktop/1' and a manifest that must contain bin/node and managed-cli/airs-cli (runtime_bundle.rs:54-78). Show from the desktop-server path that the engine does not need Node or airs-cli. Note that its shell policy resets PATH (airs_desktop_runtime.rs:242-244). Acknowledge that removing them may require engine-side changes (instructions text, pin/manifest contract), not only a new seal.

Candidate 3's test surface lists signature/issuer/audience rejection without marking signature validation as a v2 addition. v1 ADR 30 explicitly omits JWKS signature verification in the host; v1 checks iss/aud/azp/exp/iat/nonce in the TS worker. Label signature/JWKS validation as a proposed stricter v2 requirement, consistent with the handoff's 'do not blindly port omitted v1 checks', so observed and proposed are not conflated. Also cite the source for the 'device authorization' (Academy) mechanism the candidate relies on.

Candidate 2 leaves out the most direct hosted-authority coupling inside the shared shell. AppShell always mounts Topbar, and Topbar's ThemeToggle persists theme through hosted trpc.settings.update (use-theme-preference.ts:17-18), which is why app-shell.test.tsx mocks tRPC. The shell barrel that packages/ui re-exports wholesale also exports AppearanceSync (settings.get) and NotificationsBell (notifications.*). packages/ui/package.json declares Clerk, tRPC and router as dependencies. Name these explicitly: 'non-Academy screens trigger no learner effects' depends on theme persistence not being a learner-account mutation in desktop.

Not every handoff exploration priority is covered or explicitly dispositioned. Priority 6 (explicit outcome/freshness/completeness semantics and import/rollback across local work) and parts of priority 3 (protected-storage and Academy learner-account identity schemes) and priority 4 (typed host tools, protected history) have no candidate and no recorded reason for exclusion. Add candidates or state why no real friction point was found, with source evidence.
optional_suggestions: Fix minor line-anchor drift: request.rs:557 is the doc comment and MAX_IN_FLIGHT is at :559; rail.tsx:50 points at sectionActive rather than the brand/route embedding (lines 81-97, 156-160); airs_desktop_runtime.rs:155 is developer_instructions, so cite the bootstrap/identity binding at :280-287 if that is the intended claim.

In candidate 4, note that a same-origin redirect may keep method and body (307/308), and that cross-origin managed redirects return the 3xx response (attempt.stop()) rather than an error. Both affect what 'denial before secrets reach an unauthorized transport' must test.
Note in candidate 3 that ADR 31 records workspace MCP as verified only with fakes and a literal runtime, not against an authenticated Gateway, so retained MCP behaviour is fixture-level evidence.
Candidate 2 could note that packages/ui is private and exists for Claude Design tooling (index.ts:1-6), supporting the shallow-module claim, and that PreviewProviders is the only package-owned code.
Consider labelling the HTML Mermaid 'Proposed delivery relationship' as non-selected, as the footer does, to avoid it reading as a chosen dependency graph.
The recommendation order 'take all four' is presented as a recommendation pending owner selection, which is appropriate. Keep it phrased that way until the owner decides.
limitations: Scoped review of G01 candidate research only. It does not complete G01, does not requalify the old G00 plan, and selects no candidate, interface, ADR or outbound licence.
